techStack: Express v5, ESM project ('type': 'module'), TypeScript strict (noUnusedParameters, noUnusedLocals)
Custom error hierarchy: AppError → ProductNotFoundError (404), RateLimitError (429), ValidationError (400), DatabaseError (500), AuthError (401) — all in src/errors/index.ts
RateLimitError constructor: RateLimitError(retryAfterSeconds: number) — stores readonly retryAfterSeconds, hardcodes statusCode=429, code='RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED', message='Too many requests'

Centralized errorHandler: 4-arg Express middleware, checks instanceof RateLimitError first (sets Retry-After header, returns 429), then AppError subclasses (returns statusCode + {error, code, requestId}), then generic 500
Test framework: Vitest + supertest; run with 'pnpm test' (vitest run); test files under src/benchmark-backend/dist/tests/visible/
features: favouriteController.ts:add — catch block checks 'err instanceof ProductNotFoundError' and calls res.status(404).json({ message: 'Product not found' }) — inline response bypasses errorHandler; other errors call next(err) correctly
compareController.ts:compare — catch block calls next() with NO argument, swallowing the error silently; Express treats this as 'no error' and falls through to 404 handler

rateLimiter.ts — constructs plain new Error('Rate limit exceeded, retry after Xs') and passes to next(); errorHandler has no branch for plain Error with rate-limit semantics, falls through to generic 500
rateLimiter.ts already computes retryAfterSeconds as Math.max(1, Math.ceil((oldest + 60000 - now) / 1000)) — value is always >= 1
rateLimiter.ts already has /health bypass guard: if (req.path === '/health') { next(); return; } — must not be touched
Test files: rateLimiter.test.js, favourites.test.js, compare.test.js, auth.test.js, middleware.test.js, pagination.test.js, products.test.js, userProfile.test.js
architecture: Middleware chain in app.ts: requestId → rateLimiter → routes → controllers → errorHandler (last)
Controllers call next(err) to reach errorHandler; any bare next() or inline res.send() bypasses it
RateLimitError must be imported from '../errors/index.js' (ESM .js extension required for local imports) in rateLimiter.ts
Files that must NOT change: src/benchmark-backend/src/middleware/errorHandler.ts, src/benchmark-backend/src/errors/index.ts, all files under src/benchmark-backend/src/services/
edgeCases: favouriteController.ts:add — after fix, only next(err) must be called in the ProductNotFoundError catch branch; no res.status/res.json call for that branch; other-error branch already calls next(err) and must be preserved

compareController.ts:compare — caught error variable must be passed to next(); either 'err' or '_err' naming is acceptable (TypeScript noUnusedParameters does not flag used underscore-prefixed vars); bare next() is the bug
rateLimiter.ts — retryAfterSeconds is already Math.max(1, ...) so it is always >= 1; pass this exact computed value to new RateLimitError(retryAfterSeconds); do not recompute or hardcode it
rateLimiter.ts — /health bypass (next(); return;) must remain unchanged; fix only touches the rate-limit-exceeded branch
errorHandler responses for AppError/RateLimitError always include {error, code, requestId} — the inline 404 in favouriteController only has {message}, which is the observable difference tests check
Rate-limit boundary: 100th request succeeds, 101st triggers the >= MAX_REQUESTS branch — no change to threshold logic, only the error type constructed

tasks.requirement: 1 — favouriteController.ts:add must call next(err) for ProductNotFoundError, not send an inline response
tasks.description: In the add handler's catch block, remove the 'if (err instanceof ProductNotFoundError) { res.status(404).json({ message: ... }) }' branch and replace it with 'next(err)' so the error reaches errorHandler regardless of its type. The else branch calling next(err) for other errors can be collapsed into a single next(err) call.

tasks.requirement: 2 — compareController.ts:compare must call next(err) (with the caught error), not next() with no argument
tasks.description: In the compare handler's catch block, change 'next()' to 'next(err)' (or 'next(_err)' if the variable is underscore-prefixed). The caught error must be passed as the argument so errorHandler receives it and can return the correct status code and JSON body.

tasks.requirement: 3 — rateLimiter.ts must construct a RateLimitError instance and pass it to next(), not a plain Error
tasks.description: Import RateLimitError from '../errors/index.js' at the top of rateLimiter.ts. In the rate-limit-exceeded branch, replace 'next(new Error(...))' with 'next(new RateLimitError(retryAfterSeconds))' using the already-computed retryAfterSeconds value. The plain Error construction and its message string can be removed.
